A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoGPA work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison after matching pagination changes and retained qualitative examples.

before.justification: V2 reports original video-generation experiments in Table 1, a human preference study in Figure 3, and quantitative ablations and generalization experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and reports revised Wan2.2 results and additional VideoReward measurements in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The reconstruction-derived preference score, candidate filtering, v-prediction DPO objective, and LoRA alignment procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The backbone revision in Table 13 concerns evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions retain DL3DV-10K, WebVid, Panda-70M, I2V/T2V tasks, and the same dynamic qualitative scenarios. Both already evaluate Wan2.2 under scripted camera-motion prompts and natural CogVLM2 captions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the base models, SFT, Epipolar-DPO, and GeoVideo in their respective comparisons. Table 13 still compares Wan2.2 with VideoGPA, and the appendix optimization and runtime comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 13 changes the reported natural-caption reprojection evaluator from VGGT to DA3-Large, giving both Wan prompt regimes a common evaluator. It also extends reported metric coverage with VideoReward breakdowns. The PDFs do not establish retraining or changes to the evaluated sample counts.

E4.justification: Appendix G revises the evidence testing transfer from scripted training prompts to natural captions on Wan2.2, replacing geometric results and adding perceptual and motion-quality measurements. The training-step, optimization-strategy, backbone-agreement, label-noise, OOD, and qualitative analyses elsewhere are retained.

E5.justification: The three-seed candidate-generation description and Table 6's plus/minus summaries are unchanged. No new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures appear.

E6.justification: Table 13 replaces natural-caption results: baseline/VideoGPA PSNR changes from 15.103/14.388 to 24.06/24.41 under a different evaluator, precluding a same-setting performance comparison. New natural-caption VideoReward VQ/MQ/TA/OVL scores are 47/67/45/56%; scripted OVL of 57% was already reported in v2's prose. Section 4.2 corrects I2V 3DCS from the erroneous 0.579-to-0.551 claim to 0.485-to-0.483 and GeoVideo MVCS from 0.852 to 0.819, matching the unchanged Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same DPO derivations, projection and reconstruction definitions, consistency loss, and motion-filter formulas. No formal assumption, proof, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the advertised plausibility benefit from physical to geometric, accompanied by descriptions of alignment with geometric rather than physical laws. The central claims of data-efficient, self-supervised geometric alignment remain.

C2.justification: Appendix G replaces the interpretation that geometric alignment is not the bottleneck under natural captions with an interpretation of modest benefits there. V4 acknowledges increased Epipolar error while retaining camera motion as the strongest regime. The motion-manifold explanation and long-video scalability limitation remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 adds a direct project-website link and clarifies in Tables 8, 10, and 11 that DA3-Large applies to reprojection-based metrics. Table 4 loses its explicit VGGT-1B footnote, although its caption still identifies VGGT. These disclosures do not establish new code availability or changed training.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Du et al.'s A Cookbook of 3D Vision and its reference entry. The positioning relative to geometric foundation models and alignment methods otherwise remains unchanged; the Ho et al. reference update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized terminology and editorial corrections, shortens the conclusion's limitation paragraph, adds a cross-reference to the existing Wan evaluation, and rewrites and reverses the prompt-regime discussion in Appendix G. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 13 gains four VideoReward columns, reverses its prompt blocks, and revises its caption and evaluator note. Other table notes and spacing change locally. Figures and qualitative examples are retained, although many Appendix I images have lower embedded resolution, and the references spill onto a mostly empty page.

improvement.justification: V4 improves accuracy by reconciling Section 4.2 with Table 1 and improves transparency through a common reprojection evaluator and fuller VideoReward reporting in Table 13. These limited gains outweigh the minor presentation drawbacks. The stronger natural-caption interpretation still requires qualification: Epipolar error worsens, and visual-quality and text-alignment win rates are 47% and 45%. The revision therefore improves reporting more than it strengthens the underlying scientific evidence.
